facts.text: PEGASUS, VVM, SET Level, VaViM and EVIDENT are publicly funded research programs, mostly German and Swedish, that developed scenario- and simulation-based validation of automated driving; their durations indicate how long building such a capability takes.
facts.quote: These are the publicly funded research programs, mostly German and Swedish, that worked out how to validate automated driving with scenarios and simulation, and whose durations show how long building such a capability takes.

facts.text: PEGASUS was a German project that defined a method for validating a Level 3 highway automation function.
facts.quote: PEGASUS was the German project that defined a method for validating a Level 3 highway automation function.

facts.text: PEGASUS ran from 1 January 2016 to 30 June 2019, a duration of 42 months.
facts.quote: It ran from 1 January 2016 to 30 June 2019, 42 months

facts.text: PEGASUS involved 17 partners, about EUR 34.5 million in funding including EUR 16.3 million in public subsidy, and about 1,791 person-months, roughly 149 person-years.
facts.quote: with 17 partners, about EUR 34.5 million (EUR 16.3 million public subsidy) and about 1,791 person-months, roughly 149 person-years.

facts.text: PEGASUS produced a validation method, not a certified product, including a scenario database built from field recordings, simulation, proving-ground tests and field tests.
facts.quote: It produced a method, not a certified product: a scenario database built from field recordings, simulation, proving-ground and field tests

facts.text: PEGASUS produced the three-level scenario idea—functional, logical and concrete—that later entered the ISO 3450x standards.
facts.quote: the three-level scenario idea (functional, logical, concrete) that later entered the ISO 3450x standards [Chapters 2, 9].

facts.text: PEGASUS partners included car makers, suppliers, simulation vendors and test laboratories.
facts.quote: Its partners included car makers, suppliers, simulation vendors and test laboratories [Chapter 2].

facts.text: VVM (Verification and Validation Methods) was the follow-on project for urban Level 4 and 5 automation.
facts.quote: VVM (Verification and Validation Methods) was the follow-on for urban Level 4 and 5 automation

facts.text: VVM ran from July 2019 to June 2023 with a EUR 47 million project volume.
facts.quote: July 2019 to June 2023, with a EUR 47 million project volume

facts.text: VVM stated a goal of a “significant shift from real tests to simulation.”
facts.quote: the stated goal of a "significant shift from real tests to simulation" [Chapter 2].

facts.text: SET Level, a sister project to VVM, published the Credible Simulation Process in August 2021.
facts.quote: SET Level, a sister project, published the Credible Simulation Process (August 2021)

facts.text: SET Level's Credible Simulation Process embeds simulation credibility in product development and ties credibility levels to the criticality of the simulation task.
facts.quote: which embeds simulation credibility in product development with credibility levels tied to the criticality of the simulation task

facts.text: The booklet treats SET Level's Credible Simulation Process as a process template, not as proven off-road.
facts.quote: the booklet treats it as a process template, not proven off-road [Chapter 10].

facts.text: The Swedish VaViM program ran from February to August 2022 with Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Blekinge Institute of Technology, funded through Vinnova and Drive Sweden.
facts.quote: VaViM (February to August 2022; Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Blekinge Institute of Technology, funded through Vinnova and Drive Sweden)

facts.text: VaViM studied validation of virtual models for autonomous vehicles in fenced areas and built a feasibility model.
facts.quote: studied validation of virtual models for autonomous vehicles in fenced areas, built a feasibility model

facts.text: VaViM planned simple comparative physical tests.
facts.quote: planned simple comparative physical tests

facts.text: VaViM concluded that validated models and real tests must be used side by side.
facts.quote: concluded that validated models and real tests must be used side by side

facts.text: VaViM's six-month duration sufficed for a pre-study, not an accepted capability.
facts.quote: six months "sufficed for a pre-study, not an accepted capability" [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The Swedish EVIDENT program ran from April 2022 to December 2024, about 33 months, with SAFER and Vinnova.
facts.quote: EVIDENT (April 2022 to December 2024, about 33 months, SAFER and Vinnova)

facts.text: EVIDENT researched credible virtual verification, correlation, and replacing or complementing real recordings.
facts.quote: researched credible virtual verification, correlation and the replacement or complementing of real recordings

facts.text: EVIDENT 2 was still running in 2026.
facts.quote: EVIDENT 2 was still running in 2026 [Chapter 2].

facts.text: Based on PEGASUS, VVM, SET Level, VaViM and EVIDENT, the booklet's central timeline finding is that building the validation capability took years in every documented case.
facts.quote: The booklet's central timeline finding rests on these programs: "building the capability took years in every documented case"

facts.text: The booklet concludes that a four-month window must be used as a validation window, not a capability-construction window.
facts.quote: so a four-month window must be a validation window, not a capability-construction window [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The booklet identifies VaViM as the nearest precedent for off-road machines.
facts.quote: VaViM is the nearest precedent for off-road machines

facts.text: VaViM supports using automotive credibility concepts for off-road validation without assuming that automotive sensor and environment models are valid off-road.
facts.quote: supports using automotive credibility concepts without assuming automotive sensor and environment models are valid off-road [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The booklet uses PEGASUS, VVM, SET Level, VaViM and EVIDENT as a reference class for schedule forecasting.
facts.quote: The booklet also uses these programs as a reference class for schedule forecasting [Chapter 12].
